brief.reader: English-speaking reader who recognizes Dockerfile RUN but needs image-layer semantics explained.
brief.question: Why does later deletion hide a file without removing its earlier image-layer bytes?
brief.takeaway: Later deletion adds a mask; same-RUN cleanup avoids adding a NEW temporary file's payload to the resulting diff.
brief.medium: Three-scene deterministic SVG video source, 1280x720; not a completed video.
brief.direction: Dark opening, light mechanism and comparison by default. Exact host Clawpilot variables and first detection script; Segoe UI/Aptos stack; explicit scoutTheme overrides remain possible.
brief.motionResponsibilities: Lower a newly created file into layer A; reveal an upper whiteout and remove only the merged-view example path while leaving lower payload visible; contrast that with a temporary file moving into deletion before the same RUN's resulting diff.
brief.captionReserve: All authored explanatory content ends by baseline y540; y550–720 is reserved for runtime burned captions.
brief.labelSizes: Primary labels 32px or larger; sources and scope notes 18px. Actual font substitution and clipping remain untested.

segments.text: Suppose one RUN adds a hundred-megabyte file: its payload enters an immutable image layer.
A later RUN hides the file with a whiteout, but the earlier layer still holds its bytes.
Create and delete that new file within the same RUN, and its payload never enters the resulting image diff.

narration.proposedDisclosureScope: If separately approved in the future, transmit only these exact narration strings to the Edge TTS service, not source code, research snapshots or review notes. No voice/network consent exists and nothing has been transmitted for speech.
narration.timingStrategy: Requested measured total is 20–30 seconds. A roughly 25-second editorial target is only a planning estimate, not Aria timing evidence. Future approved audio measurements determine segmentFrames at 30 fps; each source scene derives local progress solely from those supplied frames. If measured speech falls outside the approved range, revise and seek fresh complete-plan approval rather than silently time-stretching or editing hashes.
narration.sentenceCaptions: One caption segment per scene; the 19-word longest segment still requires actual three-line overlay fit inspection.

factualReview.condition: The file is NEW, remains after the first successful RUN and is part of an ordinary unsquashed image diff.
factualReview.observation: Source copy says 'Suppose' and labels file payload, not image total. The footer explicitly marks 100 MB as assumed uncompressed and excludes base/overhead.
factualReview.limit: Not a measured build, compression ratio, network transfer, cache usage or physical-storage result.

factualReview.locator: later-delete narration; upper-layer, merged-empty and fixed lower payload
factualReview.condition: Whiteout semantics apply to a lower path in the layer stack.
factualReview.observation: The authored SVG keeps file.bin in the lower image-layer cutaway while the merged-view copy is replaced with 'file.bin is absent'. The whiteout is drawn only in layer B, not as an ordinary merged-view file.
factualReview.limit: Source correspondence only. No pixels or kernel behavior observed.

factualReview.condition: New temporary path absent before and after the same RUN; no squashing or special mounts.
factualReview.observation: Narration says 'that new file' and 'resulting image diff', avoiding a claim that the entire image or layer is empty. The comparator retains the separate-RUN lower payload.
factualReview.limit: Directory metadata or other outputs may still persist. Deleting preexisting base content does not reclaim lower blobs.

conditions: The title identifies Docker, a deleted file and retained bytes without needing the prompt.
The first segment identifies the file and immutable layer; the second supplies masking as the reason for changed visibility without changed lower storage.
The final segment changes exactly one condition: whether the NEW temporary file crosses a RUN/diff boundary.
The whiteout technical term has the adjacent visible label 'deletion marker' and a mask bar, instead of introducing a wall of unfamiliar terms.
Spatially separate merged view, layer B and layer A; the persistent lower payload is not faded away with the deleted merged path.
Scope footers identify illustrative payload and avoid exact image-total labels.
